title: Gin Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: GET /hello calls this handler. Context.String sends formatted text with a status. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Gin calls the matching GET handler with a context. String sends status 200 and the greeting. Use a matching HTTP method and path.

exercises.question: gin.H is a short map type for named data. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: gin.H creates a named map. JSON serialises it and writes the requested status. Use c.JSON so the response has the right content type.

exercises.question: A colon marks a route value. GET /hello/Ravi puts Ravi in the name parameter. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Param reads Ravi from the named path part. String inserts it into the %s slot. A route value is text until it is parsed and checked.

exercises.question: DefaultQuery reads a query parameter and supplies a fallback. GET /page uses the text fallback 1. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: DefaultQuery reads no n value and uses the string 1. JSON therefore quotes it. Query values are strings, even when they look like numbers.

exercises.question: strconv.Atoi turns text into an int or reports an error. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Atoi successfully parses 4. The handler then returns its doubled value. Always check the parse error before using the number.

exercises.question: ShouldBindJSON reads and checks JSON fields. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: ShouldBindJSON fills the struct through its pointer and checks required Title. The valid result is returned with 201. Pass a pointer so the binder can fill the struct.

exercises.question: A group gives related handlers a common path prefix. Open GET /api/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The api group adds /api to /books before matching the route. The group prefix belongs in the requested URL.

exercises.question: Middleware can set request values before calling the next handler. Open GET /school. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The middleware stores a context value, then calls Next. GetString reads it in the route. Request context values belong to the current request.

exercises.question: Header sets a response header. Open GET /note and inspect Cache-Control. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Header sets Cache-Control before String writes the body. Set headers before writing the response body.

exercises.question: Redirect asks the client to visit a new URL. GET /start ends at /hello in a browser. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Redirect sends status 302 and the target URL. The next GET reads the greeting. A redirect is a second client request.

exercises.question: NoRoute supplies a fallback handler. GET /missing has no normal route. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: No regular route matched, so the NoRoute handler sends its controlled 404 reply. Keep the 404 status even with a friendly body.

exercises.question: AbortWithStatusJSON stops later handlers in the chain. GET /closed receives this practice block message. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: AbortWithStatusJSON writes the error and stops later handlers. The second handler is not called. Abort stops later handlers but does not return from the current Go function.
